whatContradictedTheCard: Gap ledger section 9 states a cad-null-verified semantic would NOT close Williamson improvement because those values 'exist under a different key' -- framed as a join-miss case. That framing does not hold against the live store: the identity join hits the R-prefix CAD row at rate 1.0 (gap ledger section 7), so the R-prefix row IS the matched row for a Williamson landing parcel, and its improvement/living/assessed fields are null ON THAT MATCHED ROW while the numeric sibling row (different prop_id) holds the dollar values. The dispatch's own negative fixture is therefore a join-miss shape (value under a different key that never matches) which is NOT what live Williamson does. This seat's inherited CP1/CP2 work already caught and resolved this: it implemented the dispatch's structural row-level rule as specified (not an R-prefix runtime skip, which the dispatch forbids), added test (b) as the card's literal join-miss fixture, and added test (b2) as the live Williamson match-hit shape, explicitly named so PARCEL-R6B does not read a moved Williamson improvement cell as proof the join-miss scoping leaked -- it proves the card's fixture and the live store are different shapes, and the emission is working as designed on both. No code decision changed as a result; the finding is that the emission WILL touch Williamson improvement/living once R6B re-ingests, and that is correct per the ruling's own text ("basis records the CAD row itself"), not a scope violation.

LESSON: Gap-ledger sizing sections describe the CAD store's key shape at a point in time; a module's structural scoping should be verified against the live join behavior (here: R-prefix identity join rate 1.0), not just the ledger's prose description of which class a semantic would or would not close.

A card's 'negative fixture' description in prose (join miss) and its live equivalent (match-hit with a null field) are different structural shapes and both need a test -- the second one is often the one that actually fires in production.
